A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BID study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including the proofs moved from Appendix C in v2 to Appendix D in v3.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original diagnostic simulations, seven robot-manipulation simulation tasks, two real-world robot tasks, and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original simulation and real-world results and adds VQ-BeT component ablations and distance-metric experiments in Appendices A.5–A.6.

M1.justification: The default BID algorithm, backward coherence, and forward contrast remain unchanged. V3 adds evaluated L1 and cosine alternatives to L2 distance-based sample scoring in Appendix A.6, providing limited inference variants without changing the architecture or training objective.

E1.justification: The manipulation benchmarks and real-world tasks remain the same. Diagnostic environmental coverage changes from noise levels 0.0, 0.4, and 0.8 to 0.0, 0.2, and 0.4 in Section 5.1 and Table 3.

E2.justification: V3 adds EMA to the VQ-BeT Push-T comparisons in both open-loop and closed-loop operation (Table 4), alongside component variants. EMA previously appeared in other experiments, but v2's VQ-BeT comparison included only vanilla sampling and BID.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1.2 changes the reported VQ-BeT sampling temperature from 0.1 for vanilla and 0.5 for BID to 0.5 for all methods. This revises an experimental control within retained coverage; the PDFs do not establish that temperature alone explains the replaced results.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 examines backward coherence and positive/negative forward-contrast components for VQ-BeT across noise levels and execution modes. Appendix A.6 adds distance-metric sensitivity tests on Square, Lift, and Kitchen. Together these substantially extend evidence about component contributions and robustness beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: V3's Table 4 adds numerical plus/minus uncertainty entries to the VQ-BeT comparisons previously reported as point estimates. Their statistical meaning and experiment-specific run counts are not specified. Existing three-seed reporting for the main Diffusion Policy experiments is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 replace substantial numerical results, and Tables 4–5 add component and metric results. For example, Table 1's closed-loop BID success at noise 1.5 changes from 54.4% to 31.7%; the revised protocol prevents treating this as a demonstrated same-setting deterioration. The main Diffusion Policy and real-world findings remain.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 moves actions available only to the longer-horizon policy from the conditioning set into the variables averaged over. Appendix D adds equality conditions to Propositions 6–7 and a new Proposition 9 with a proof relating observation advantages to inference-error bounds. These are substantive formal changes beyond relocating and renumbering proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: analyzing the consistency–reactivity tradeoff and introducing BID to improve action chunking. The claimed coverage and headline relative improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses why fixed-horizon action chunking may scale differently from option discovery and how larger datasets might mitigate long-context policies' spurious correlations. Appendix A.6 interprets metric alternatives as further potential for BID. The principal computational and short-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies that prediction length equals action horizon in Appendix A.2 and that Figure 5's policies share a prediction length. It also revises the VQ-BeT temperature instructions. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments; existing code links, hardware, and training-budget descriptions remain.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit comparison with model predictive control. New Appendix C expands positioning relative to option discovery, long-context learning, and robotic foundation models, with corresponding citations. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V3 clarifies prediction length versus action horizon, rewrites selected explanatory passages, and adds an additional-discussions appendix before the proofs. Most of the main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with explicit observation, prediction, and replanning steps. Figure 5 replaces overlaid density curves with separate probability histograms. V3 adds Tables 4–5 and renumbers the retained hyperparameter table as Table 6; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: Using a common VQ-BeT temperature removes a comparison confound, while the new component and metric tests strengthen empirical support. Clearer horizon terminology also helps interpretation. The theoretical additions are not an unqualified gain: Appendix D.5 newly states that alpha_f vanishes when P_f=0, conflicting with D.1's P_f=1 condition. Overall, the experimental and explanatory gains support a modest improvement despite this inconsistency.
